title: Returns and bargaining
persona: You are a polite shop assistant at an electronics store in Sydney. Store policy: refunds need a receipt; faulty items can be exchanged.
briefTr: Dün aldığın kulaklık arızalı. Fişin çantanda. Önce mağazada iade et, sonra Paddy's Markets'ta bir bumerang için pazarlık yap.
opening: Hi there! How can I help?

facts.question: What was the seller's first price?

goals.instruction: The customer says they want to return an item because it is faulty.
goals.hint: I'd like to return these headphones. They're faulty.
goals.hintTr: Bu kulaklığı iade etmek istiyorum. Arızalı.
goals.retryReply: Is there a problem with something you bought?
Do you have the receipt with you?

goals.ask: Would you like an exchange or a refund?
goals.instruction: The customer says whether they want a refund or an exchange.
goals.retryReply: Would you like your money back or a new pair?

goals.ask: Handmade boomerangs! Have a look, love.
goals.instruction: At the market, the customer asks the price.
goals.retryReply: Want to know the price, love?
goals.persona: You are a cheeky market seller at Paddy's Markets in Sydney selling handmade boomerangs. You enjoy bargaining but you won't go below forty-five dollars.

goals.instruction: The customer asks for a lower price.
goals.hint: It's lovely. Can you do a better price?
goals.hintTr: Çok güzel. Daha iyi bir fiyat yapabilir misiniz?
goals.retryReply: Is that price okay for you?

goals.instruction: The customer makes a counter-offer with a number.
goals.successReply: Ha! Meet me in the middle.

goals.instruction: The customer accepts the final price or politely says no.
goals.retryReply: So, have we got a deal?

twists.intro: Hmm, this receipt is from a different store, actually.
twists.instruction: The receipt is wrong. The customer looks for the right one, offers the card statement, or asks for an exchange instead.

options.text: Let me look for the right one.
options.reply: Take your time… yes, that's the one!

options.text: Can I show my card payment instead?
options.reply: That works — I can see it here.

options.text: Then could I just exchange them?
options.reply: Sure, an exchange is fine without a receipt.

twists.intro: We can only give you store credit, not cash.
twists.instruction: The store offers only store credit. The customer refers to the faulty product, asks for an exchange, or asks for the manager.

options.text: But they're faulty, so I should get a refund.
options.reply: You're right, for faulty items it's a full refund.

options.text: Then I'll take a new pair.
options.reply: Here's a brand new pair. They work fine.

options.text: Can I speak to the manager?
options.reply: She says a refund is fine. Sorry for the trouble.

twists.intro: The box has been opened, so we need to test them first. Can you come back tomorrow?
twists.instruction: The store wants to test the item. The customer asks to test it now, explains they are leaving, or agrees.
twists.retryReply: It's quick, but our tech is out today.

options.reply: Okay, let me plug them in… yep, faulty. Refund it is.
Ah, then I'll do it now. Here's your refund.
Thanks. Actually — I can see the problem. I'll refund you now.

twists.intro: Nah, sixty's a fair price, mate. Can't go lower.
twists.instruction: The seller refuses. The customer says they will look around, offers to buy two, or explains their budget.

options.text: Okay, I'll have a look around first.

options.reply: For you — fifty. Don't tell anyone!

twists.intro: Just so you know, I only take cash.
twists.instruction: The seller only takes cash. The customer asks for an ATM, offers to pay by phone, or checks their wallet.
twists.retryReply: Most stalls here are cash only.

options.text: Can I pay with my phone?

twists.intro: Oh — that one's got a small chip on the end.
twists.instruction: The item has a defect. The customer asks for another one, asks for a lower price, or says it's fine.

options.text: Then can you make it cheaper?
